visualReview.notes: Original2026-10-10 pixel inspection retained after exact generator/output checks; no new rendering or architectural change. Actually inspected all 16 portable frames, 16 shared-material frames and 32 medium-fi frames after the final Heel Stone taper. The complete ensemble, fallen pieces, unreconstructed west gaps, three complete inner trilithons, two broken groups, outlying stones and bank remain present. Close detail views confirm asymmetric shoulders, taper, fallen-stone profiles and exposed tenon without the decorative profile bands caught in the earlier render. Overview frames cover the whole asset; intentionally close lintel cameras clip peripheral stones. The exposed Altar Stone is mostly obscured by fallen pieces, consistent with the described current condition.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Two canonical 256px shared stone graphs bind to sarsen and mixed bluestone approximations, with meter-based UVs and no embedded images. Actual shared views show subdued off-white stone with fine repeat, avoiding copied lichen photographs or unique maps. Both graphs were read once, and unload disposed the model with zero live geometry. The grass bank uses a plain local palette. The basalt graph is a stylistic stand-in for diverse bluestone geology; it is not a mineral identification.

mediumFiReview.notes: Actually inspected every noon/late, economy/high, silhouette, authored detail and four-level transition frame. The pale stone palette remains consistent with the synthetic procedural context. Context houses are a scale/style fixture, not evidence of houses at Stonehenge. All levels preserve the exposed ensemble; the skyline bank is visibly polygonal at a deliberately closer transition inspection, bounded by a conservative 2.1m whole-asset error. District, street and closeup progressively refine the bank and stone profiles without adding missing ancient stones.

geographicReview.notes: Fresh attributed OSM four-outlier controls were rigidly fitted to the inspected English Heritage current plan, retaining its scale. Heel, Slaughter and Station 91/93 centers constrain a maximum 1.127m residual; anchor [-1.8262310128,51.1788579596], heading 0.013739514043 rad gives native +X almost east and +Z almost south. The Heel Stone to the northeast resolves the signed pose. Actually inspected the north-up placement overlay against the whole earthwork outline: the 32m stone circle is not stretched to the 120m enclosure. Accepted tolerance is 5m and 2 degrees for plan/map generalization. GroundY0 uses the central contact plane; absolute height and real terrain slope are unmeasured, and footprint replacement remains disabled.

fidelityReview.notes: Primary current-site plan, English Heritage description, published laser-report text and survey-team paper informed a complete exposed stone-and-earthwork medium-fi interpretation. Seventeen outer upright parts, six outer lintels, three complete inner groups, two isolated inner uprights, fallen pieces and visible bluestones are represented. Exact individual stone-number registration, measured contours, carved marks, geology, local tilt and below-ground sockets are not claimed. The current-plan page was inspected separately from ancient reconstruction phases; unavailable laser-report image pixels were not treated as inspected evidence. The old schematic draft recipe remains byte reproducible, while this full current-condition recipe is now the authored source.

legacyFidelityScope.notes: The lit image uses regular straight blocks and a schematic ring. Actual stone profiles, surviving versus missing lintels, individual locations and current-site orientation remain unresolved.
legacyFidelityScope.reviewBinding: Historical record only; current approval is the newly inspected medium-fi scope.

tests.command: Selected generator reproduced identical GLB, spec, preview scene and README; source document set unchanged (canonical list order refreshed). Six validation/LOD hashes, placement, shared graphs and all64 previously reviewed image hashes verified unchanged.

geometryValidation.notes: Three focused tests pass: exact old-draft reproduction and current source reproduction; independent geometry probes for the current groups, gaps, outliers, low bank and open bays at all four levels; deterministic LOD bytes, signed placement and separate 12-byte POSITION/NORMAL streams. All six GLBs pass the Khronos validator with zero errors and zero warnings. The 55,452-triangle master has 86 exposed stone parts and low earthwork. Triangle side normals were corrected during review; the final validator ran after that correction and the Heel Stone taper.

runtimeLodReview.notes: Four pinned browser derivatives: skyline 904 triangles / 97,560 bytes, district 3,900 / 416,420, street 8,312 / 910,400 and closeup 55,452 / 6,485,544. Initial skyline plus district is 513,980 bytes, below both phone and laptop download targets. Skyline has one draw, other levels three. Authored geometry and shared graph bindings survive upgrades, and all six validated binaries match recorded hashes. Physical device timings and real sloping terrain placement remain unmeasured; the review establishes byte/geometry budgets and browser fixture correctness.

limitations: Complete static medium-fi interpretation of the current surviving Stonehenge ensemble: seventeen outer sarsen uprights including the short fragment, six surviving outer lintels, three complete inner trilithons, two isolated inner uprights, fallen sarsen fragments, visible bluestones and stumps, a mostly obscured Altar Stone, Heel Stone, Slaughter Stone, both surviving Station Stones and low bank/ditch earthwork surface. Missing ancient stones and lintels are not reconstructed. Layout and condition were read from the current English Heritage2015 plan; above-ground profiles, heights, local tilts, fragmentation and joint dimensions are authored photographic interpretations, not survey meshes or exact stone-number identification. The first draft recipe remains unchanged and independently reproducible. Four browser levels retain every authored stone and the bank; chamfering and surface tessellation increase toward closeup. A shared sandstone graph stands in for sarsen silicified sandstone, and common raw basalt stands in for mixed bluestone geology. Lichen, carvings, graffiti and particular mineral grains are not copied. Plan controls and raw OSM stone outlines disagree locally because generalized aerial top outlines are not ground surveys; four distinct outlying stones constrain a rigid fit with no scale change. Registration tolerance5m/2Â° acknowledges this. Bank height and ditch depth are relative interpretations; the runtime host supplies absolute terrain and its slope may occlude or expose the setting. Below-ground sockets, buried fragments, excavation markers, fences, access paths, full Avenue, visitor center and the wider World Heritage Site are outside the exposed stone-and-earthwork asset. Physical phone/laptop timing is unmeasured.
